facts.raw_span: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms

concepts.why: The patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, severely decreased ejection fraction, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation are all indicative of advanced heart failure.
The patient's low blood pressure, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation suggest cardiogenic shock.
The patient's heart rate of 106 beats/min and the ECG findings of regular atrial tachycardia at cycle length 320ms support the diagnosis of atrial tachycardia.
The patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, decreased ejection fraction, and the ECG findings of wide QRS rhythm at ~100 beats/min support the diagnosis of ventricular tachycardia.
The patient's history of amiodarone treatment and the severely decreased ejection fraction suggest amiodarone-induced cardiomyopathy.

aliases: Ischemic Heart Disease with Atrial Fibrillation
concepts.why: The patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and the ECG findings of atrial tachycardia support the diagnosis of ischemic cardiomyopathy with atrial fibrillation.

The patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, severely decreased ejection fraction, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation are all indicative of biventricular heart failure.
The patient's severely decreased ejection fraction and the signs of substantial volume overload support the diagnosis of systolic heart failure.

aliases: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
concepts.why: The patient's history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation are all indicative of diastolic heart failure.

The patient's worsening shortness of breath, New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation are all indicative of acute decompensated heart failure.

The presence of a single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator in a patient with worsening heart failure symptoms and confirmed dual tachycardia suggests potential malfunction or inadequate therapy.

rationales.F01: History of ischemic cardiomyopathy suggests advanced heart failure and systolic heart failure.
rationales.F02: Ejection fraction of 25% indicates severe left ventricular dysfunction, consistent with advanced heart failure and systolic heart failure.
rationales.F03: Single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator is often used in patients with severe left ventricular dysfunction, increasing the likelihood of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator malfunction.
rationales.F04: Worsening shortness of breath is a common symptom of advanced heart failure and acute decompensated heart failure.
rationales.F05: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms indicate severe limitation of physical activity, consistent with advanced heart failure and acute decompensated heart failure.
rationales.F06: Amiodarone treatment previously may be associated with amiodarone-induced cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F07: Heart rate of 106 beats/min may indicate atrial tachycardia or ventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F08: Blood pressure of 96/58 mm Hg may indicate cardiogenic shock.
rationales.F09: Elevated jugular venous pressure is a sign of right-sided heart failure, consistent with advanced heart failure and biventricular heart failure.
rationales.F10: Bilateral lung crackles on auscultation indicate pulmonary congestion, consistent with advanced heart failure and acute decompensated heart failure.
rationales.F11: Prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation is a sign of left ventricular volume overload, consistent with advanced heart failure and systolic heart failure.
rationales.F12: Ejection fraction of 10% indicates severe left ventricular dysfunction, consistent with advanced heart failure, systolic heart failure, and ischemic cardiomyopathy with atrial fibrillation.
